title: A read can be answered at several layers; the earlier, the cheaper
caption: Each layer keeps its own copy. The closer to the user, the faster the hit, and the harder it is to invalidate.

steps.text: The browser's HTTP cache answers repeat visits with zero network: images, scripts, and anything sent with Cache-Control.
A CDN keeps public, static content (media, bundles) close to users, often 10-50 ms closer than your region.
An in-process cache costs no hop at all (~100 ns), but each of your servers holds its own copy, and the copies drift.
A shared in-memory cache is one copy for all servers, about 0.5 ms away. This is the layer interviews usually mean.
Only misses reach the database (5-50 ms per query). Every hit above is load it never sees.
